PullRequest.Title: ci: run Monaco Editor checks only on pull requests
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

This PR removes the `push` trigger (`main` and `release/*`) from the **Monaco Editor checks** workflow (`.github/workflows/monaco-editor.yml`). The `pull_request` trigger for `main` and `release/*` is unchanged. Nothing else in the workflow changes.

## Why

- **Duplicate runs after merge.** On every push, the workflow re-ran the same ~5 minute check (Monaco compile check, `monacodts-check`, editor distro, ESM check, typings validation, webpack bundle, editor tests) that the commit's PR had already passed. `main` gets about 70 pushes a day.
- **The push trigger was inherited, not chosen deliberately.**
  - d9fb87d002d (2019, "CI for Monaco Editor compile and bundling.") added the Monaco job to the old all-in-one `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. That workflow ran everything on both `push` and `pull_request`.
  - d1e59b8fc53 (2022, "Move Monaco Editor checks to a separate GH action") moved the job into `monaco-editor.yml` and copied the `on:` block verbatim from `ci.yml`. The commit message gives no reason for keeping `push`.
  - 454208e1135 (2025) deleted `ci.yml`. The only later edit to the trigger block added `permissions: {}` (15807c660e6).
- **The post-merge runs haven't caught anything the PR runs missed.** All of the last 100 push runs on `main` succeeded. The four most recent failures were all the "Run Editor Tests" step hanging until its 5-minute timeout. Each one was on a commit whose PR run had passed, and the next push passed:
  - https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/39052524263 (f4e47b2c7b, #342302)
  - https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/38829156804 (e963f2347a, #341878)
  - https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/38633351876 (73534d499f, #341629)
  - https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/37541062861 (fcb34e1259, #340105)
- **Nothing else depends on these runs.** No Azure Pipelines step runs `monaco-compile-check`, `monacodts-check` or `editor-distro`, and this workflow is not a required status check on `main`.

## Behavior change

- Pushes to `main` no longer run this workflow.
- Pushes to `release/*` also stop running it. PRs into `release/*` still run it, just like PRs into `main`.

## Validation

- **YAML parse and trigger check: passed.** This uses `js-yaml` from `build/node_modules` to compare the workflow against `origin/main`:

  ```sh
  git show origin/main:.github/workflows/monaco-editor.yml > /tmp/monaco-editor.before.yml && node -e '
  const assert = require("node:assert/strict");
  const fs = require("node:fs");
  const yaml = require("./build/node_modules/js-yaml");
  const before = yaml.load(fs.readFileSync("/tmp/monaco-editor.before.yml", "utf8"));
  const after = yaml.load(fs.readFileSync(".github/workflows/monaco-editor.yml", "utf8"));
  assert.deepEqual(Object.keys(after.on), ["pull_request"]);
  assert.deepEqual(after.on.pull_request, before.on.pull_request);
  assert.deepEqual(after.on.pull_request, { branches: ["main", "release/*"] });
  const strip = ({ on, ...rest }) => rest;
  assert.deepEqual(strip(after), strip(before));
  console.log("OK: YAML parses; on =", JSON.stringify(after.on), "; all other keys unchanged");
  '
  ```

  Output: `OK: YAML parses; on = {"pull_request":{"branches":["main","release/*"]}} ; all other keys unchanged`
- **Docs check: nothing to update.** I searched `.github/` (instructions, skills, agents), `.agents/`, `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `README.md`, `build/monaco/` and `test/monaco/` with `rg`. Nothing says the Monaco checks run on push or after merge, so no docs changed.
- **Pre-commit hygiene hook (`npm run -s precommit`): passed.**
- No build or tests were run, since this change only edits the workflow trigger.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Each merge to main or release/* generated a second heavyweight Monaco CI run after the pull-request run, repeating dependency/cache/network setup and all compile, bundle, and test subprocesses.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Unnecessary post-merge runner time, subprocess work, network/cache traffic, and potential GitHub Actions queue contention on every matching push.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The workflow now triggers only for pull requests to main or release branches, eliminating one full post-merge CI job per matching branch push while preserving the pre-merge check.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Base line 4 registered `push` for main/release branches in addition to the unchanged pull_request trigger. The same workflow contains a single job that checks out the repository, restores or installs dependencies, downloads Playwright, runs multiple Monaco compile/distribution/type checks, bundles with webpack, compiles tests, and runs tests. Thus merging a checked PR caused another full run of the same heavyweight job on the resulting branch push; the PR deletes that push trigger while retaining PR validation. Blame identifies the trigger as introduced by d1e59b8fc534fd31a0065820f8697bab503ec28c.

Scenarios.Scenario: Pull request targeting main or release/* runs Monaco Editor validation before merge
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The unchanged pull_request event starts the workflow; checkout, dependency preparation, Playwright download, compile/distribution/type checks, bundling, compilation, and tests must complete for this workflow to succeed. The diff does not add, reorder, or delay any step on this path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Checks out repository state, obtains toolchain/cache data, conditionally installs packages/system dependencies, and downloads Playwright artifacts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per pull-request workflow invocation, with npm/system installation conditional on the node_modules cache miss; Playwright installation remains once per run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same boundaries ran once for the PR event before the diff; their PR-event cardinality and placement are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These setup operations precede and therefore gate Monaco checks for the PR.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Runs Monaco compile and declaration checks, editor distribution/ESM checks, TypeScript validation, webpack bundling, test compilation, and editor tests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One serial sequence per pull-request workflow invocation; no per-file or per-project fan-out is introduced by this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same serial command sequence ran for the PR event before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All commands are on the workflow success critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One workflow invocation per qualifying PR event; cost scales with PR event frequency and the existing repository build/test workload, neither of which is increased by the diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One `main` job runs per pull_request workflow invocation. Its listed steps execute serially; repository checkout, cache operations, package setup, builds, and tests are not fanned out by this diff. Separate PR workflow invocations remain independently scheduled by GitHub Actions, with no changed concurrency setting.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing node_modules and npm caches retain their existing keys and behavior. A warm node_modules cache skips npm/system dependency installation; misses perform those steps. The trigger removal does not change keys, coalescing, or negative-cache behavior for retained PR runs.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the pull_request trigger and all job steps are unchanged in the complete diff and full workflow.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact runtime and cache hit rates vary, but the diff provably adds no work to this scenario.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: PR validation behavior and its expensive boundaries are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Push or merged commit lands on main or release/*
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Before the diff, the branch push immediately scheduled the full Monaco workflow; after the diff, no Monaco workflow work is on this event path. The removed work was asynchronous to product execution but consumed CI runner capacity.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: .github/workflows/monaco-editor.yml deleted `push` trigger reaching job `main` setup steps
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: For every matching push, checked out the repository, accessed caches, conditionally installed npm/system dependencies, and downloaded Playwright artifacts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before: once per push to main or release/*, with install work dependent on cache state. After: zero calls from those push events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every matching branch push invoked this setup sequence; the diff removes the invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The operations consumed CI runner/network capacity but did not gate the already-completed merge itself.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Ran the complete serial compile, declarations, distribution, ESM, typing, webpack, compile, and test sequence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before: one complete sequence per matching push. After: zero push-triggered sequences.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One full job ran per matching push; the diff eliminates it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The sequence occupied a runner and could contribute to Actions queue contention, but was off the branch-push critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The removed cost scaled linearly with the number of pushes to main and release/*; absent a concurrency group, bursts could occupy multiple runners concurrently.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Previously, each matching push independently scheduled one full `main` job, potentially overlapping jobs from nearby pushes because the workflow defines no concurrency group or cancellation. After the diff, effective concurrency for push-triggered Monaco jobs is zero.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Previously each push still performed checkout, cache lookup, Playwright installation, and all build/test commands; warm caches could avoid npm/system dependency installation but did not eliminate the job. After the diff there is no cache lookup or cold/warm distinction for push events.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: deleting the only push trigger makes the full job unreachable from branch pushes, and no other changed files or trigger paths exist.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact push frequency, job duration, and cache misses are deployment-dependent, but direction and one-job-per-push cardinality are explicit in the workflow.
Scenarios.Verdict: Performance improvement, not a regression: the diff removes repeated CI setup and subprocess work. The originating trigger was recorded as a regression fix.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete one-file diff and full workflow. The only change deletes push triggers for main and release/* while retaining pull-request validation unchanged. It introduces no performance regression; it removes one heavyweight, uncancelled CI job per qualifying push. No findings were submitted, and the traced repeated-work fix was recorded against its introducing commit.
